source.citation: Periscope summary of a report to a medical society in Turin (Dr. Antonio [surname unclear in OCR]) on Flechsig's opium-bromide method in ten cases of epilepsy, Case 3, Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease 23 (1896): 345.
source.place: Turin, Italy (reported in an American journal)

complaints: general convulsive attacks at irregular intervals
sometimes followed by days of mania
presentation.course: Epileptic for five years, since a fright from nearly drowning.

treatments.treatment: opium from January 20, 1895, increased to 50 centigrams a day

treatments.response: no further attacks noted to the end of July

outcome: Free of attacks for about four months at the time of the report.
quotes: has been an epileptic for five years, following fright from danger of drowning
the bromides were sub- stituted, and no further attacks were noted

modernReading.text: Epilepsy. Fright was a common period explanation; the near-drowning could instead have injured the brain through lack of oxygen, or be coincidence. Bromides do reduce seizures but cause dullness and skin eruptions in long use.

fixed: an event the patient or family blames for them

constrained.rule: one where a seizure is dangerous or costs the job raises the stakes

notes: Not a New York case. An American epilepsy case should replace or join it.
